acceptedFindings.title: Data and code not provided, analysis unreproducible
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without access to the underlying data (raw or synthetic), the exact analytic steps, and the complete environment, the results cannot be independently verified, which is essential for scientific integrity and external validation.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide the dataset in a repository or as supplementary material, along with a fully executable analysis script and a codebook that defines all variables.

acceptedFindings.title: Manuscript does not report PCA outcomes or answer the research question
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without any results or interpretation, the study is fundamentally incomplete and cannot be evaluated.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Update the manuscript to include the proportion of variance explained, component loadings, and an interpretation of the latent components. Reference the scree plot and discuss component retention.

acceptedFindings.title: No interpretation of components provided
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The primary output of PCA is the component structure; without interpretation, the research question remains unanswered.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: In the discussion, interpret the loadings: PC1 appears to load heavily on the three scale items, suggesting a general factor; PC2 is dominated by severity. Discuss what this implies about the latent structure.

acceptedFindings.title: Variable definitions and data source missing
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Readers cannot interpret the PCA loadings or assess the validity of the measures without knowing what 'scale_item_1–3' and 'severity' represent, their scales, and their provenance.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Include a detailed description of each variable (type, range, units), the instrument or source they were derived from, and any relevant psychometric properties in the Methods.

acceptedFindings.title: Cohort construction not described
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The generalizability and internal validity depend on how participants were selected and which exclusions were applied. The statement 'read from available run artifacts' is opaque.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Specify inclusion/exclusion criteria, the total eligible pool, how missing data were handled, and any thresholds for complete-case analysis. Report a participant flow diagram.

acceptedFindings.title: PCA pre-processing (scaling/centering) not specified
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: PCA is sensitive to variable variances; loadings and explained variance depend on whether the correlation or covariance matrix was used. Without documentation, interpretation is unreliable.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: State explicitly whether variables were standardized (z-scored) before PCA, and justify the choice (e.g., correlation matrix used because variables have different scales).

acceptedFindings.title: No assessment of data suitability for PCA
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: PCA requires adequate correlations among variables. Without KMO, Bartlett's test, or checking for ordinal structures, the analysis may be inappropriate, especially if items are binary or ordinal.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin measure, Bartlett's test of sphericity, and consider whether polychoric correlations are needed for ordinal items. Discuss sample size adequacy.

acceptedFindings.title: PCA misrepresented as latent variable analysis
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: PCA is not a latent variable model; it does not account for measurement error and assumes components are linear combinations of observed variables, not latent constructs. This mischaracterization may lead to incorrect clinical interpretation.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Change terminology to 'component structure' or switch to an exploratory factor analysis model. If latent constructs are intended, use EFA with an appropriate extraction method and rotation.

acceptedFindings.title: No interpretation of PCA results provided
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The manuscript merely lists variance explained and loadings without any discussion of what the components represent, their clinical or research meaning, or how they relate to the original research question.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Interpret each retained component based on loadings (>0.4 or 0.3), label them meaningfully, and relate them to the study objective. Include the scree plot with a description of retention criteria (e.g., Kaiser rule, parallel analysis).

acceptedFindings.title: No uncertainty measures or formal component retention criteria
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Component emphasis (e.g., PC1 explains 79%) is presented without confidence intervals, and the number of components to retain is not justified, making the solution appear more stable than it may be.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Include bootstrap confidence intervals for eigenvalues or explained variance, report parallel analysis results, and discuss the rationale for retaining components (e.g., scree plot, >1 eigenvalue, cumulative variance).

acceptedFindings.title: Variables not described
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The reader cannot assess the meaning or quality of the variables, undermining the interpretability of the PCA.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add variable descriptions: what do scale items 1-3 and severity measure? What are the units, possible ranges, and reliability estimates?

acceptedFindings.title: No PCA suitability diagnostics reported
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without checks like KMO, Bartlett's test, or determinant of correlation matrix, it is unclear if PCA is appropriate for these data.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Run and report standard PCA diagnostics (KMO measure of sampling adequacy, Bartlett's test of sphericity, communalities, check for multicollinearity). Include them in the diagnostics file and manuscript.

acceptedFindings.title: No descriptive statistics or distribution checks
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: PCA is affected by outliers, skewness, and variable scaling. Without summary statistics, the plausibility of the input data cannot be assessed.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide univariate summary statistics (mean, SD, range, skewness) for each variable. Report any transformations or scaling applied before PCA.

acceptedFindings.title: Data not available for reproducibility
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The analysis is based on a local dataset that is not shared, making independent verification impossible.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Deposit a de-identified minimal dataset or synthetic data with the analysis artifacts, or clearly state data availability restrictions.

acceptedFindings.title: Figure QA file is empty
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The scree plot may have quality issues not automatically checked, potentially misleading component selection.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Populate figure-qa.json with checks for axis labels, title, legibility, and verify that the scree plot is correctly referenced in the manuscript.

acceptedFindings.title: Manuscript is overly generic and lacks study-specific content
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Most of the text is boilerplate that does not reflect the specific analysis, reducing clarity and specificity.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Replace generic placeholder text with details tailored to this PCA analysis, including the specific research context and findings.
